methodologyNotes: Roster covers 12 CPAP/APAP/bilevel machines a 2026 buyer typically compares: ResMed AirSense 11 AutoSet, ResMed AirSense 10 AutoSet, ResMed AirMini AutoSet, ResMed AirCurve 11 VAuto, Philips DreamStation 2 Auto CPAP Advanced, React Health Luna G3, React Health Luna II (G2), Apex Medical iCH Auto, Fisher & Paykel SleepStyle, Löwenstein prisma SMART, Somnetics Transcend Micro, and Somnetics Transcend 3. Primary sources were manufacturer/official pages where reachable (reacthealth.com, loewensteinmedical.com, mytranscend.com, usa.philips.com, ap.resmed.com) plus authorized-dealer and reviewer pages (thecpapshop.com, cpapsupplies.com, cpapstoreusa.com, gocpap.com, sleepfoundation.org, sleepapnea.org, cpap.am) when the manufacturer's own eshop blocked automated fetches. IMPORTANT CORRECTIONS/CLARIFICATIONS vs. the seed list: (1) Philips DreamStation 2 Auto CPAP Advanced — the official Philips product page explicitly states "Not for sale in the United States"; per the April 2024 FDA/DOJ consent decree, Philips Respironics has not sold new CPAP/BiPAP devices in the US since January 2024 and there is no confirmed resumption date, so priceUsd is null (not a guess) even though the device is still widely discussed/compared and second-hand units remain in circulation. (2) Löwenstein prisma SMART — the manufacturer's own site notes its product range "may vary from country to country" and shows no US pricing or US distributor; Löwenstein sells primarily through European/international channels, so priceUsd is null. (3) "3B Medical Luna II" — 3B Medical rebranded to React Health in 2023; the current official product page and the device's own front-panel silkscreen both read "Luna II" / model G2, listed here as React Health Luna II (G2). (4) "Apex Medical iCH Auto" — several US retailers market current stock as "iCH II Auto," but the unit's own front-panel branding and the retailer's technical spec table both read "iCH Auto"; treated as the same continuously-sold product. (5) Somnetics Transcend 3 miniCPAP Auto — a retailer (CPAP Store USA) flags this model as discontinued in 2023 and Somnetics' own current comparison page (mytranscend.com/compare) no longer lists it, only the newer Transcend Micro line; kept in the roster (per the seed list) as a widely-compared legacy travel CPAP, with pricing reflecting remaining retail inventory rather than an active MSRP. (6) React Health Luna G3 — one retailer (CPAPsupplies.com) marks this SKU discontinued/superseded by a "Luna G3 X," though React Health's own product page was still live with no such notice at access time. Noise-level dB figures are each manufacturer's own quietest-condition rating (e.g. ResMed/Philips/Apex test methodology); independent reviewer testing can read higher in real-world use (e.g. Transcend Micro reviewed at up to 31 dB without its optional WhisperSoft muffler vs. the 27 dB rated figure). Weight figures are for the base flow-generator unit as stated by the cited source (accessories/power supply may add weight). All prices are US-market figures; a null price means no current USD manufacturer or retail price could be verified, not that the product is unpriced elsewhere. All research accessed 2026-08-01.

products.name: ResMed AirSense 11 AutoSet
products.priceNote: ResMed's official eshop.resmed.com lists the AirSense 11 AutoSet with HumidAir and standard tubing (base config) at $1,054.00 ($1,096.00 with ClimateLineAir heated tubing); The CPAP Shop, an authorized dealer, sells the same base config at $1,004.00.

specs.humidifier_type: Integrated heated humidifier (HumidAir) with automatic climate control
specs.data_connectivity: Wireless (Wi-Fi/cellular) to myAir app and AirView cloud platform
specs.mask_compatibility: Universal — works with any standard CPAP mask

products.provenance: The CPAP Shop's product page (fetched directly) gives the full spec set used here: 4–20 cmH2O pressure, integrated heated humidifier with ClimateControl Auto, 27 dBA noise, 2.5 lb weight, wireless connectivity via myAir (with Apple Health/Health Connect sync), Sleep Onset Detection ramp, universal mask compatibility, and automatic altitude compensation. Direct automated fetches of eshop.resmed.com returned HTTP 429 (bot-protection), but the exact official page text — including the $1,054.00 base price and $1,096.00 ClimateLineAir bundle price — was independently retrieved and quoted verbatim by a search pass, and the product's identity/design was separately confirmed by viewing ResMed's own AP healthcare-professional product image (touchscreen unit with HumidAir tub, ResMed logo), which is used as the image asset. No explicit release date was found on any consulted page; ResMed launched the AirSense 11 as the successor to the AirSense 10 but the exact date is not stated on the fetched pages, so releaseDate is null.

products.name: Philips DreamStation 2 Auto CPAP Advanced
products.priceNote: No current USD price exists: the official Philips product page states verbatim "Not for sale in the United States." Under the April 2024 FDA/DOJ consent decree following the 2021 PE-PUR foam recall, Philips Respironics has not sold new CPAP or BiPAP devices in the US since January 2024, with no confirmed resumption date as of this research.

specs.machine_type: APAP (Auto CPAP), switchable to fixed CPAP mode
specs.humidifier_type: Integrated adaptive heated humidifier (325 mL tank, 5 humidity settings, 5 temperature settings)
specs.mask_compatibility: Universal — standard 15mm/22mm tubing connector, works with any CPAP mask

products.provenance: Fetched directly from Philips' own US product page, which explicitly confirms US unavailability and gives: 4–20 cmH2O pressure range, CPAP/Auto CPAP modes, automatic altitude compensation, Ramp Plus (15/30/45 min), FLEX pressure relief, 325 mL adaptive humidifier tank (5 humidity + 5 temperature settings), weight 1.04 kg (2.3 lb) without accessories / 1.34 kg with power supply, 256.8×158.5×84.8 mm dimensions, integrated cellular modem + Bluetooth, and a 2-year warranty. Independent coverage (cpap.com) corroborates the ≤27 dBA rating (rising to ~29 dB with the humidifier active) and 325 mL tank capacity. The image is Philips' own product photograph (images.philips.com), which Philips itself overlays with a "Product currently unavailable in US" banner — direct visual confirmation of both product identity and market status. No release date was stated on the fetched page; the DreamStation 2 line is known to have launched around 2020 but that is not explicitly sourced here, so releaseDate is left null.

products.name: ResMed AirMini AutoSet
products.priceNote: ResMed's official eshop.resmed.com lists the AirMini AutoSet machine (no mask bundle) at $919.00; The CPAP Shop, an authorized dealer, matches this exactly at $919.00 (regular price $999.00).

specs.humidifier_type: Waterless HumidX heat-and-moisture-exchange system (no water tank)
specs.data_connectivity: Bluetooth to the AirMini app; syncs to ResMed AirView cloud (no built-in Wi-Fi/cellular)
specs.mask_compatibility: Proprietary — requires AirMini-specific HumidX setup packs (AirFit P10/N20/N30/F20, AirTouch N20/F20); not usable with standard masks without one

products.provenance: The CPAP Shop's product page (fetched directly) confirms: 4–20 cmH2O, waterless HumidX humidification, <30 dB noise (ISO 80601-2-70:2015 rating of 29 dBA ±2 dBA per ResMed's own fact sheet), 10.6 oz (0.66 lb) weight, Bluetooth app connectivity with AirView cloud integration, AutoRamp, and the mask-compatibility caveat that AirMini requires its own HumidX setup packs rather than standard masks. Direct WebFetch of eshop.resmed.com returned HTTP 429/405 repeatedly, but the official $919.00 price was independently retrieved and quoted verbatim by a search pass against that exact page, and it matches The CPAP Shop's price exactly. The image (ap.resmed.com, ResMed's own Asia-Pacific site) was visually confirmed to show the compact AirMini unit. No release date found on consulted pages; ResMed introduced AirMini publicly in 2016 but that is not sourced here, so releaseDate is null.

specs.data_connectivity: Bluetooth to the SleepStyle mobile app

products.name: Somnetics Transcend Micro Auto CPAP
products.priceNote: Current price on the manufacturer's own store (mytranscend.com) is $769.00 against a listed regular price of $1,099.00; independent reviewers (Sleep Apnea Association) show it at $779.

specs.machine_type: APAP (Auto CPAP), switchable to fixed CPAP mode
specs.humidifier_type: Waterless AirMist HME (heat-and-moisture exchanger); no integrated water tank
specs.data_connectivity: Bluetooth to the MySleepDash app (24hr/7-day/30-day/90-day compliance reports)
specs.mask_compatibility: Universal — works with any mask with a standard 22mm connection

products.provenance: Manufacturer product page (mytranscend.com, fetched directly) confirms: 4–20 cmH2O range, waterless AirMist HME humidification, 27 dB noise (ultra-quiet rating), 0.48 lb weight, 3.6×3.6×2.4 in dimensions, MySleepDash app connectivity, GentleRise ramp (5–45 min), AirRelief (EZEX) pressure relief, universal 22mm mask compatibility, automatic altitude adjustment up to 8,000 ft, FAA compliance, and current/regular pricing of $769/$1,099. SleepApnea.org's independent review (fetched directly) corroborates the 4–20 cmH2O range, GentleRise ramp, universal mask compatibility, MySleepDash connectivity, and a $779 price, but records noise at 26 dBA rated / 31 dB measured at 10 cmH2O without the optional WhisperSoft muffler — noted here as the discrepancy between rated and unmuffled real-world noise. The product image (fetched directly from mytranscend.com and visually confirmed: round white unit branded "transcend") is the manufacturer's own photography. No release date found on either page.
